todo: Obtain qualified-human citation verification for the proposed Arnold-Chiari malformation to sleep-apnea association.

Confirm the Chiari phenotype, separately diagnosed sleep apnea by polysomnography, obstructive versus central phenotype, chronology, airway findings, decompression history, and competing sleep-disordered-breathing causes before publication.

suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-34 adds this relationship only as a bounded Chiari-associated sleep-disordered-breathing association. A pediatric case report describes obstructive sleep apnea in Arnold-Chiari malformation with polysomnographic resolution after posterior-fossa decompression, but a single case does not establish that every sleep-apnea diagnosis in a person with Chiari malformation is caused by the malformation. Require independently documented Arnold-Chiari malformation, separately diagnosed sleep apnea by polysomnography, explicit obstructive or central phenotype characterization, compatible chronology, and neurology and sleep-medicine review. Preserve adenotonsillar or upper-airway obstruction, obesity, craniofacial anatomy, pulmonary disease, medication effects, and other causes.
evidenceGaps: Independent MRI documentation of Arnold-Chiari malformation and clinically relevant brainstem or upper-airway findings
Separately established sleep apnea by polysomnography with obstructive, central, or mixed phenotype specified
Chronology, sleep-study severity, oxygenation or hypercarbia, airway evaluation, and decompression response
Assessment of adenotonsillar disease, obesity, craniofacial anatomy, pulmonary disease, medications, and other causes
Neurology and sleep-medicine assessment of the individual relationship

sourceReferences.citation: Katwa U, Sisniega C, McKeon M, Lee GS. Sleep endoscopy-directed management of Arnold-Chiari malformation: a child with persistent obstructive sleep apnea. J Clin Sleep Med. 2020;16(2):325-329. PMID 31992420. doi:10.5664/jcsm.8194.
sourceReferences.note: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-34 case-based clinical evidence for the bounded Chiari-associated sleep-apnea proposition. Mapping approval is not citation verification; this source remains pending qualified-human review.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 31992420; pediatric case with polysomnographic obstructive sleep apnea and resolution after posterior-fossa decompression; approved ME-34 guard requires independent sleep-study phenotype review.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Chiari malformation can coexist with sleep-related breathing disorders, and the cited pediatric case reports obstructive sleep-apnea resolution after decompression, but case evidence does not establish an individual nexus without phenotype, chronology, and competing-cause review.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR section 3.310 is established; the mapping is a bounded clinical association and not an individual nexus opinion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Cerebellar tonsillar or brainstem crowding may affect respiratory control or sleep-dependent upper-airway and vocal-cord function, but the relevant obstructive or central pathway remains hypothesized for an individual until MRI, polysomnography, airway evaluation, and neurologic review are integrated.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. The source is a pediatric case report with a treatment response and cannot establish that Chiari malformation caused sleep apnea in every individual.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Chiari imaging and phenotype; polysomnographic classification; chronology; airway and respiratory findings; decompression response; and review of obesity, upper-airway anatomy, pulmonary disease, medications, and other sleep-disordered-breathing causes.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Pulmonary disease or neuromuscular respiratory weakness
